invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.

Every changed page works fully without JavaScript: every state change is a form post, every search and filter a form with a button that submits it, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 6; conflicts:c-006).

A behaviour is built with GOV.UK Frontend first, then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype, pop-ups are not built and confirmations stay pages (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 5, 7 and 19).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.

A search box is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select and behaves as the real frontend configures it; its entries are what MDM serves through reference-data, and only how the list reads follows the prototype (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 1 to 4).

Where a row changes a page or behaviour the high-risk plants frontend also has, the same increment changes plants too: plants mirrors the structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and keeps its own questions, data and step order (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 43 and 44).
Shared wording in a frontend's shared copy is never reworded in place; a set-specific string goes in the feature's own copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 41).

Notification statuses are only ever added, never renamed or removed, and each new status is mapped in every frontend that reads it before the animals backend first sends it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 42).
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).
'Save and return to overview' saves without the page's required-answer checks, but still refuses an answer that fails its own format rule (conflicts:c-211; ruling:sam-2026-10-07).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

increments.title: Live-animal commodity catalogue matches Design Release 2.1
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1's named live-animal catalogue: 0102 as 'Cattle' with 11 species, Horse with Donkey and Mule, 'Domestic cat' and 'Domestic dog', Ferret and Other live mammals on 01061900, Ornamental fish in place of Fish, and the poultry, livestock, rabbit, camel, ostrich, parrot, reptile and bee commodities. Dropped by the 2 November re-analysis: every one of those names and species lists is prototype demo data, and the catalogue's content is MDM's. See the notes.
acceptanceCriteria: Dropped. The live-animal catalogue is whatever MDM serves through reference-data, which the frontend has read since EUDPA-617 merged on 27 October. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 25; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 28 and 30)

sources.ref: prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-109 to -p2-132, -p2-134, -p2-135, -p2-137, -p3-026, -p3-027 (all kind 'data', from app/data/commodities.js and app/data/commodities-0102-species.js)
ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-025 (claim 25: a list's content is what MDM serves)

notes: Confirmed by the 2 November re-distil, which read the V4 data fields page in full for the first time. V4 says the catalogue's content is MDM's, in its own words: 'The Commodity selection values come from the named MDM commodity list' and 'Commodity selection's values come from MDM' (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-070, -p1-073), 'Species selection's values come from MDM' (-p1-089) and 'Type selection's values come from MDM' (-p1-081). So the drop no longer rests only on claim 25 of the 9 October ruling: the specification itself defers the catalogue to MDM. The re-distil's own pick-up list still carries req-094 to req-101 as 'Blocked on MDM commodities' with Design Release 2.1's wording ('0102 is named Cattle, not Cow', 'Cattle offers DR2.1's 11 species', 'Ornamental fish (030111) replaces Fish'), but that judgement was made against a repo extract taken on 26 October, the day before EUDPA-617 landed, so it describes a catalogue of five hard-coded stub commodities that no longer exists. Not applied.

What V4 does not settle, and this row therefore does not either: V4's example commodity selection reads 'Cattle, 0102, Bos taurus' (confluence-6497338582-p1-075), which assumes a trader-facing commodity name, while saying the values come from MDM - and MDM serves no name in any field. So the naming question stands as a design question rather than a row. It is in deferred.md.

Dropped by the 2 November re-analysis, correcting that re-analysis's own first pass, which kept the row blocked on a commodity-naming question. The correction: claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09 says every reference list 'is built now against reference-data as it is, and its content is what MDM serves. Where a list's content differs from Design Release 2.1, that is MDM's content to change, never a reason to block a row or edit a list in code.' Claim 28 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm carved commodities out of that only 'until commodities come from MDM', and said that once they do, 'the area is re-distilled'. They came on 27 October (frontend c3183a8e), so the carve-out has expired and claim 25 governs the commodity catalogue as it already governs countries and ports.

What that means for every criterion this row used to carry: the named commodities ('Cattle', 'Pig', 'Domestic cat', 'Domestic dog', 'Ferret', 'Other live mammals', 'Ornamental fish'), the 11-species cattle list, the three horse species and the rest are all list content, so they are MDM's to change and never a reason to block a row or edit a list in code. The provenance confirms they were never requirements: every claim behind them is kind 'data', extracted from the prototype's own hard-coded demo files at commit 04a073b - app/data/commodities.js:10-25 for the commodity names and app/data/commodities-0102-species.js:3-15 for the cattle species. They were written to make the prototype's pages demonstrable, not to specify a catalogue. The prototype's declared role covers 'every page, field, option, hint, error message, branch and journey step'; a reference list's contents are not in that set, and ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 2 says so directly - 'List entries: they are whatever MDM serves through reference-data', with only 'how the list reads' following the prototype, and then only 'wherever the component can show them'.

Camel and ornamental fish are not a data gap and never blocked anything. Neither is in MDM's GBN-AG dataset - there is no 010613 or 01061300 in the chapter-01 tree and a search for 'fish' returns nothing - and under claim 25 that is MDM's content. Fish is correct as it stands rather than missing: live aquatic animals are not a GBN-AG live-animal commodity, and fish is managed under the IUU regime, not this service. Camel is a content request to MDM if anyone wants it, recorded in deferred.md.

The commodity heading is the bare CN code on main, because reference-data's CommodityGroup carries only a code and a list of species and MDM holds no trader-facing commodity name in any field - its commodity rows carry a CN tariff description ('Live bovine animals', 'Other', 'other than. 0106 14 10'), and animalSubcategory, natureOfCommodity and breedCategory are empty on all 49 rows in the capture. Under claim 25 that is the honest outcome of MDM's content, not a defect in the frontend, and under claim 2 the component cannot show a label MDM does not serve. Whether a bare CN code is good enough for a trader is a design question, and whether MDM should serve names is a content request; both are recorded in deferred.md, and neither is work for this theme.

Not dropped because it is built: dropped because the requirement was prototype demo data. The one real consequence left is outside this theme. EUDPA-669 sends the commodity name downstream to PIMS as the trade line description and falls back to the bare CN code for 23 of the 26 codes (fix/EUDPA-669-commodity-name-code-type:src/server/app/services/persistence/records/notification-mapper/mapper-a/commodity.js:27, and its COMMODITY_NAMES_BY_CODE of three entries). If a CN code is not acceptable as a PIMS trade line description, that is EUDPA-669's to settle, with a content request to MDM behind it.

req-1919 (the k6 search term moving off 'Cow') was met on main before this row was dropped: perftests origin/main:src/config/test-data.js:5 already searches 'Bos taurus', and MDM returns nothing for 'cow'. req-112 (which commodities ask for a number of packages) moved to inc-024, which is a service rule rather than list content and so survives this drop.

increments.title: Commodity search results sorted and bolded, and a selected panel of removable species chips
increments.detail: The server-rendered commodity page lists results alphabetically with the matched text in bold, and shows what has been chosen as one bold commodity line followed by a chip per species, by Latin name, each with its own remove button, so a trader can drop one choice without clearing everything. This is how the list reads and behaves, not what is in it: the entries are whatever MDM serves (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 2), and only the reading follows the prototype. Ruling 2026-10-09 afternoon blocked these four until commodities came from MDM; they came on 27 October, so the row goes ahead. The rest of the old row (the error on the search field, the soft Save and return, clearing the unweaned answer) moved to the commodity wording row and goes ahead.
acceptanceCriteria: Search results list commodities alphabetically by commodity name, and the species under each alphabetically by their label ('common name (Latin name)', or 'commodity name (Latin name)' where a species has no common name). (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-084, prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-109; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-026)

The text that matched the query is shown in bold in the commodity header and the species labels, such as 'Domestic **cattle** (Bos taurus)' for 'cattle'. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-024, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-028)

The selected panel lists each chosen commodity as a bold commodity line followed by one chip per chosen species showing its Latin name, such as '0102:' then 'Bos taurus'. The line reads as whatever reference-data serves for the commodity, which today is its CN code. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-035, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-041, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-023; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p1-056)

Each chip has a remove button whose accessible name is 'Remove <Latin name>', such as 'Remove Bos taurus', which takes that one species out of the selection and leaves the others chosen. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-036, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-074, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-023; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p1-060)

Without JavaScript the Search button, its results, the chips' remove buttons and Clear all all work by posting the page. (trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p8-010; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p1-060; c-012)
Every new English string, such as the 'Remove' accessible name, has its Welsh counterpart, marked as a machine draft. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p5-044)
notes: Combines the result-list slice (req-075, -076) with the selected-panel slice (req-080, -081): the same server-rendered page and view model, one review. req-085, -088 and -102 moved to the commodity wording row by ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-007 and go ahead. The chip and remove-button markup set here is what the as-you-type search row reuses, so that row depends on this one.

Re-analysis 2 Nov: unblocked. MDM was the row's only stated block and the integration is live (frontend c3183a8e, 27 Oct). Nothing this row asks for is on main. Results are not sorted: reference-data preserves MDM's order through a LinkedHashMap (referencedata origin/main:src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/commodities/CommoditySearchService.java:146-152) and the frontend groups them in encounter order (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/view-model/commodity-groups.js:17-19). The tests repo asserts that order deliberately, in a test called "groups the matching species under their commodity code, in reference-data's order" (tests origin/main:tests/animals/e2e/pages/commodities.spec.ts:45), so criterion 1 rewrites an existing test rather than filling a hole. The sort belongs in the frontend view model, not reference-data: reference-lists owns that repo.

Re-analysis 2 Nov: no text is bolded today, because the checkbox items take speciesLabel, which is the plain Latin name (frontend origin/main:.../features/commodities/species-label.js:1). The selected panel already exists and is grouped the right way but with the wrong parts: selectedSummary groups the selection by commodity code and lists its species (search/view-model/selected-summary.js:11-21), and the template renders each group as a bold legend followed by the species joined with ', ' in one list item (search/search.njk:66-73). So criterion 3's structure is half there with the bare code where the name belongs, and criterion 4 is absent entirely: there is no per-species remove control, only one 'Clear all' button (search.njk:74-79). Criterion 5 holds for what exists, since the page is one form posting to itself with Search and Clear as named submit buttons and no client-side behaviour, so the chips' remove buttons need only be submit buttons too.

Design snagging merged to main 23 Oct: the 'Select a commodity' error now always sits on the search box (SEARCH_FIELD 'commoditySearch' in search.controller.js), not on the tick boxes, and the refusal is logged. The page's Back link follows the opening run. The animals frontend has a bold-matching helper for type-aheads (src/client/common/helpers/bold-matches.js and search-fold.js, strong class app-autocomplete__match, with accent folding) and a server escapeHtml in shared/escape-html.js. Builder: reuse both for the bold matches rather than adding a third. The look of the commodity search box moved to waiting-on-design inc-014 and is not this row's.

In flight 2 Nov, EUDPA-616 (the commodity search type-ahead) is a complement to this row, not a substitute, and nothing is in flight today: all three of its pull requests were closed unmerged on 23 Oct (animals frontend #425, ins-tests #51, workspace #147) and the branch is gone from the remote, four days before EUDPA-617 rewrote the feature. Jira still says In Dev. That ticket delivers this row's criterion 2 and part of criterion 3 as a JavaScript enhancement and explicitly keeps the server-rendered flow as the no-JavaScript fallback, so it covers neither criterion 1 (alphabetical sorting) nor criterion 4 (a remove button per chip), and cannot satisfy criterion 5, which needs those buttons to work by posting the page. This row owns the server-rendered behaviour; EUDPA-616 owns the enhancement over it. Whichever lands second reuses the other's matching and emphasis. Worth quarrying from the closed frontend #425 diff: a reusable live-search macro and client module outside the commodities feature, a GET .../commodities/results route rendering the same results partial the page uses, and matching.js reporting the ranges it matched so the template renders them as <strong> with no HTML built in JavaScript.

Re-analysis 2 Nov: the earlier note that the commodity heading rule has one owner called commodities.commodityLabel, used by search/view-model/legend.js, is out of date. EUDPA-617 rewrote the feature: the owner is legendFor (search/view-model/labels.js:1), which is the identity function on the code, used by the result groups, the selected panel and, through buildCommodityGroups (features/commodities/view-model/commodity-groups.js:6), Commodity details. The selected panel's bold line should take legendFor too, so it picks up inc-012's naming decision in one place. The row's label format in criterion 1 ('common name (Latin name)') rests on inc-025, which restores the common name to speciesLabel.

increments.title: The k6 walk visits the main import reason between the commodity page and Commodity details
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 makes the two commodity pages steps of the journey rather than an overview task that returns to the overview. Save and continue on the commodity page goes on to the main import reason; Commodity details comes after the main import reason, and Save and continue goes on to identification, additional or arrival details, whichever applies first. Opened from its overview task, each page still returns to the overview. Main's opening run already gives this order. The k6 performance suite's live-animals walk visits the main import reason between the two commodity pages, so the suite keeps running. The two pages' Back links moved to design-snagging inc-218 on 20 October.
acceptanceCriteria: The k6 performance suite's live-animals walk, run against the local stack, visits the main import reason page between the commodity page and Commodity details and passes every check it makes on each page. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-051; ruling:sam-2026-10-07 ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-002; repo:perftests repo-perftests-p1-024; c-225)
notes: Unchanged in substance; ruling 2026-10-09 afternoon (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-011) confirms the commodity pages' place in the journey goes ahead on today's data. Combines the back-link slices (req-089, -108) with the next-step slices (req-087, -117, -118) and the k6 step-list slice (req-1761): the same journey flow change, observed only together, and the suite breaks the moment the order changes. c-015 (ruled): Design Release 2.1's chaining wins; opened from its overview task a page returns to the overview (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-196). c-016: both pages keep the three return controls. c-018: the no-commodity redirect stays. c-225 (ruled): the performance suite changes in each increment whose change breaks one of its k6 scripts, on that increment's branch name; its 'Cow' search changes with the blocked catalogue row (req-1919), not here. Where Commodity details goes after a change from check answers is req-119's, which the type-question-and-templates branch holds; this row does not change it. The main import reason page already exists; the reason-and-additional-details rows change its copy, not its place. Depends on inc-001 (journey-foundation), which reorders the opening run's step list in the shared flow; this row makes the pages' own back links and next steps agree. The tests repo's journey flow walks the new order.

Salvage: trade-imports-animals-frontend 3d192e94, trade-imports-ins-tests 327f280, trade-imports-performance-tests 85acbe9 on stale branch feat/EUDPA-693-design-release-2-1-commodities-and-reason; rebuild on a fresh branch from main. Take the runBackTarget seam (flow/journey-flow.js, run.js, kit.js) and the two controllers' Back links. Main's RUN_STEPS (journey-foundation) already gives the forward order, so req-087, req-117 and req-118 already hold.

Re-analysis 2 Nov: confirmed to build, and the gap has widened rather than closed. Main's RUN_STEPS runs origin, commodities, import reason, consignment details, identification, additional details (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/run.js:29-54), so the salvage note's claim that req-087, req-117 and req-118 already hold is right, and the externalDependsOn on journey-foundation inc-001 is satisfied - that theme's rows are all done and animals frontend #399 merged on 13 October. The k6 walk has not followed: LIVE_ANIMALS_STEPS.draft still visits origin, commodities, consignment-details, identification, import-reason, additional-details (perftests origin/main:src/k6/live-animals.js:166-205), the old order. So the suite walks a journey the frontend no longer offers, and this row closes that gap rather than extending the suite.

Trimmed 20 October: the commodity page and Commodity details Back-link criteria, with req-089 and req-108, moved to design-snagging inc-218 (Back during the opening run goes to the previous step and the run carries on), under Sam's ruling that already-planned work moves into design snagging. Take only the k6 walk from the salvage commits; the runBackTarget seam and the two controllers' Back links are inc-218's.
increments.gate: Walk the journey from origin to arrival details: this row moves Commodity details after the main import reason, and every row that walks the journey from here on rests on that order.

increments.title: Hard stops: means of transport on arrival details and number of packages on commodity details
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 makes the means of transport the only hard stop on 'Arrival details', because it decides whether transit countries apply; the other arrival answers can be left for later. Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling makes this animals only: plants' arrival details keeps its own rules. On commodity details the number of packages becomes a hard stop, alongside the number of animals, on each line that asks for it.
acceptanceCriteria: On the live-animals 'Arrival details', 'Save and continue' with no means of transport chosen is refused with an error on the means of transport question. (prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:162 p7-129)

On 'Commodity details', 'Save and continue' with a line that asks for a number of packages left without one is refused with an error on that line's number of packages. (prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:162 p7-139)

sources.ref: p3-063 (arrival details' own rules are animals only)

notes: Combines two hard-stop slices (req-1642 arrival, req-1643 packages): both change which answers are required to proceed, in the obligations rather than the page content, and are reviewed together. Which species ask for a number of packages is req-112 (another area); this row only makes the question required where it is asked. Existing tests that say arrival details is enforced as a whole page (transit-means-scope) change with it.

Salvage: trade-imports-animals-frontend f94b0823, trade-imports-ins-tests 120e234 on stale branch feat/EUDPA-693-design-release-2-1-commodities-and-reason; rebuild on a fresh branch from main. Take the meansRule in port-of-entry/validate.js, requiredIntegerInRange for packages in consignment-details/fields.js, numberOfPackages 'mandatory' in obligations/sections/commodities/lines.js, and the two error strings in English and Welsh. Also take the branch's tests showing the other arrival answers stay optional and a no-packages line still saves: they guard the new rules from going too far. Plants arrival details is not touched. The germinal half of req-1642 is observed in germinal-products inc-182, which already depends on this row in themes.json.
Re-distil: existing row inc-018.

Re-analysis 2 Nov: both hard stops are still absent and both salvage notes hold, with one path correction. The page moved: the means rule goes in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/port-of-entry/validate.js, not features/arrival/port-of-entry, and validate.js still composes oneOf('meansOfTransport', transportReference.meansOfTransport()) with no required rule (:46). requiredIntegerInRange is already imported in consignment-details/fields.js beside integerInRange (:1-5), so the packages half is the one-word change inside packagesValidatorsFor (:29-38) the salvage note names, now keyed off packagesApply(entry.commodityCode).

Re-analysis 2 Nov: this row's packages hard stop applies wherever packagesApply says the question is asked, so it inherits whatever inc-024 settles - it makes the question required where asked, and does not decide where it is asked. The two are separate dials on one obligation: numberOfPackages carries status 'optional', which this row changes to mandatory, and applyTo: allowListed(commodityCode, packageCountCommodityCodes, ...), which inc-024 decides (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/lines.js:54-62).

Ordering risk, recorded 2 Nov: this row has no dependency on inc-024 and is buildable now, but building it first makes main's package list blocking rather than merely present. Today a trader importing chickens sees an optional 'Number of packages (when required)' box they can leave blank; after this row they cannot continue without filling it. If inc-024 then narrows the list, that hard stop comes off again. The criterion is written to inherit the list ('a line that asks for a number of packages'), so this row stays correct either way - but whoever plays it should know it raises the cost of getting inc-024 wrong, and may prefer to take inc-024's answer first, or to land the hard stop only on the six codes the prototype and main agree on (0101, 0102, 0103, 010410, 010420, 01061900).

Design snagging merged to main 23 Oct: neither hard stop is on main yet, but both pages' code moved, so salvage commit f94b0823 will not apply cleanly. consignment-details/fields.js was split: fieldsFor now composes animalsValidatorsFor and packagesValidatorsFor, and the packages rule (still integerInRange, so optional) sits in packagesValidatorsFor. The consignment-details controller, its tests and the commodities copy files were rewritten, and its refusals now answer 400. On arrival details, port-of-entry.controller.js takes the empty option from copy.means.selectText ('Select one') and labels options through means-of-transport-label.js (Air, Rail, Road, Sea); validate.js still uses oneOf for meansOfTransport. Builder: change integerInRange to requiredIntegerInRange inside packagesValidatorsFor, add the meansRule to port-of-entry/validate.js, and add the two error strings to main's rewritten copy files by hand. Arrival-and-transit inc-028 adds the same means rule: whichever lands second reuses it.

increments.title: End-to-end proof: poultry by rail in transit
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 proves a poultry-by-rail journey end to end, with transit countries and no identification step. Today poultry cannot be chosen: the commodity list holds five stub commodities, and Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling makes poultry wait for the MDM commodity catalogue. This row proves the whole journey once Chicken can be chosen.
acceptanceCriteria: The tests repo walks a poultry-by-rail notification from create to 'Import notification submitted': origin Germany, Chicken (01051111) Gallus gallus, 'Transit' with an exit port and the Republic of Ireland as destination country, arrival by rail with a transport identification, transit through Belgium and France, a transporter and a CPH number. (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js:237-250 p4-069; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-002, p13-182)

sources.ref: p2-001, p2-005, p2-022, p2-025 (commodities from MDM)

notes: One slice (req-1656).
Tests only: the walk proves behaviour main already has, rather than needing a frontend change.

Re-analysis 2 Nov: unblocked. MDM now serves chicken, so the walk can run. MDM gives it under two codes, 01051111 ('Weighing not more than 185 g:Fowls of the species Gallus domesticus, Grandparent and parent female chicks: Laying stocks') and 01059400 ('Fowls of the species Gallus domesticus'), each with species Gallus gallus, common name 'Chicken' (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/commodities.json). Criteria 2 and 3 rest on poultry carrying no identifier, which is already true on main: COMMODITY_IDENTIFIERS covers only 0102, 0101 and 01061900, so IDENTIFIED_CODES excludes poultry and the Identification details page and its task drop out (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/rules.js:6-34). increments.title: Main import reason and Additional details keep earlier answers on a blank save, and Save and return skips required checks when amending
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 judges the main import reason task on the reason's own answers, with Additional details its own task. 'Save and return to overview' saves what is valid and returns to the overview without the page's required-answer checks, so a trader can leave part-way through. An answer that breaks its own format rule, such as an impossible exit date, is still refused, because the service cannot store it.
acceptanceCriteria: 'Save and return to overview' with no reason chosen leaves every earlier saved reason answer as it was (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-079)
When amending, the main import reason page's 'Save and return' action saves the same way and goes to the review page (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-075)

'Save and return to overview' on the additional details page with both questions unanswered shows no error, goes to the overview, and keeps any earlier answer to each question (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-071)
notes: Unchanged from the existing row. c-211 settles 'Save and return to overview': it saves without the required-answer checks, but an answer failing its own format rule, such as an impossible date, is still refused (ruling:sam-2026-10-07). increments.title: The number of packages question is pinned to the V4 Data Fields commodity list
increments.detail: Which commodities ask for a number of packages is specified by the V4 Data Fields page, whose 'Number of packages commodities' list gives 23 chapter-01 codes. Main's PACKAGE_COUNT_CODES already holds exactly those 23, so this row proves the match rather than changing it: it pins the list against the page with a test that names it, so neither a later MDM code nor a later edit can drift. It carries req-112 and the package-question criterion that left inc-012 in the 2 November re-analysis. The prototype's nine-mammal list, which that criterion was written from, is wrong and is not followed.
acceptanceCriteria: Commodity details asks 'Number of packages (when required)', hinted 'Such as crates, bags or boxes', for exactly the 23 commodity codes the V4 Data Fields page's 'Number of packages commodities' list names (0101, 0102, 0103, 010410, 010420, 01051111, 01051200, 01051300, 01051400, 01051500, 01059400, 01059910, 01059920, 01059930, 01059950, 01061410, 01061900, 01062000, 01063100, 01063200, 01063980, 01064100, 01064900), and does not ask for any other code reference-data serves. (confluence:6497338582 'Number of packages commodities (54)'; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-026, prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-027; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-022)
A test pins that list against the V4 page, naming the page, so a later MDM code or a later edit cannot drift from it unnoticed. (confluence:6497338582)

The list has one owner in the frontend, read by both the page and the check-answers applicability rule, so the question and the review agree. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p5-064, repo-frontend-p5-065)
openQuestions: Counts confirmed by the 2 November re-distil, which read the expand in full: the list holds 54 entries and its title count agrees (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-095, -p1-096). An earlier hand count of 53 was a truncated read, not a discrepancy in the page. Those 54 entries resolve to 23 chapter-01 codes, plus germinal codes 05111000 and 05119985 and egg codes 0407, 04071100, 04071911 and 04071919, which are outside the live-animals set. For comparison, the CPH expand holds 19 entries resolving to 17 distinct codes, of which 14 are chapter-01 - so the report's '17-commodity CPH list' and a hand count of 19 rows are the same list counted two ways, not a conflict.

ANSWERED 2 Nov, superseding the question below: the V4 Data Fields page settles it and main is already right. Its 'Number of packages commodities (54)' expand macro gives 23 chapter-01 codes - 0101, 0102, 0103, 010410, 010420, 01051111, 01051200, 01051300, 01051400, 01051500, 01059400, 01059910, 01059920, 01059930, 01059950, 01061410, 01061900, 01062000, 01063100, 01063200, 01063980, 01064100, 01064900 - and PACKAGE_COUNT_CODES on main holds exactly those 23. The two apparent inconsistencies raised earlier were wrong: V4 lists both 'Domestic European Rabbits' and 'Domestic Rabbits- Other' under 01061410, so excluding 01061490 is right, and it lists birds of prey, psittaciformes and game birds but not ratites or pigeons, so excluding 01063300 and 01063910 is right. The prototype's nine-mammal list is simply wrong. Full comparison: reanalysis/v4-data-fields-commodity-rules-2026-11-02.md. (confluence:6497338582)

Superseded question, kept for the record. Is main's rule right? This is a service rule about which commodities are asked a question, not reference-list content, so claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09 does not settle it the way it settles the catalogue's contents. But the Design Release 2.1 side of it is weak evidence: the prototype's per-commodity package flag sits in the same hard-coded demo data as its commodity names (app/data/commodities.js), and it is keyed to commodities MDM does not serve at these codes, so it cannot be applied literally. Main's PACKAGE_COUNT_CODES asks on 23 codes (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/rules.js:37-60), including every poultry code, 01062000, 01063100, 01063200, 01063980, 01064100 and 01064900, while omitting 01061490, 01063300 and 01063910. The prototype would not ask poultry, reptiles, parrots or bees. So the real question is a product one: for which live-animal commodities does a trader need to give a number of packages? MDM's commodity rows carry a packageType field, empty on all 49 rows in today's capture and not read by reference-data, which would be the authority if it were populated. Who acts: Sam, with whoever owns the GBN-AG payload.
notes: Raised by the 2 Nov re-analysis, carrying req-112 and inc-012's old package-question criterion. It is blocked on the ruling above, not on MDM.

inc-018 makes the number of packages a hard stop wherever the question is asked, reading the same rule through packagesApply (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/fields.js:30-38). So inc-018 can build before this row is settled: it makes the question required where asked, and does not decide where that is. Whichever lands second inherits the other's list.

In flight 2 Nov, EUDPA-669: PACKAGE_COUNT_CODES is unchanged on its branch, but its doc asserts a rationale for main's list - 'The package-count list holds the codes of the design's package-count list that MDM's live-animal data holds. Where the design named an entry by animal, the whole code is on the list' (frontend fix/EUDPA-669-commodity-name-code-type:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/docs/services.md). That explains 01061900, which is one code covering cat, dog, ferret and other mammals, but not the poultry codes, 01062000, 01063100, 01063200, 01063980, 01064100 or 01064900, which Design Release 2.1 names individually as commodities that must not be asked. So the ruling is still needed, and the doc should be corrected with it.

MDM offers no package-type options today, checked 2 Nov. packageType is an empty array on all 49 commodity rows in the capture (repos/trade-imports-stub origin/main:src/main/resources/responses/mdmProductSearchResponses.json; same in repos/trade-imports-reference-data src/test/resources/integration/mdm-product-search-0102-response.json:32), and the field is not on the /commodities?codes= endpoint reference-data actually calls, which returns only code, description, isGerminal, isSelectable and speciesCount (stub mdmProductCommoditiesResponses.json). So reading packageType would need MDM to populate it and reference-data to read it from the search response or a widened by-code response. The vocabulary would not be MDM's own either: the GBN-AG schema holds the package type as an open string from the UNECE PackageTypeCode list, UN/EDIFACT Recommendation 21, with cage and crate as its examples (repos/trade-imports-schemas schemas/core/defra-unvtd-canonical-core-v1.schema.json:511-527 and schemas/profiles/imports/gb/gbn-ag-v1.schema.json:365-379). MDM's packageType[] would therefore be a per-commodity shortlist of UNECE codes, not a list of its own.

The physical logic favours main's list over the prototype's, which weakens the prototype side further than the demo-data provenance alone does. The GBN-AG schema says the package group is optional and names the reason: 'consignments where the animals are loose-loaded (for example livestock in a single trailer compartment) omit it' (gbn-ag-v1.schema.json:283). The prototype asks for a package count on exactly the livestock that travel loose - cattle, horses, pigs, sheep, goats - and not on the commodities that really do arrive in packages: day-old chicks in boxes, bees in hives, reptiles and parrots in crates, ornamental fish in bags. The frontend's own hint says 'Such as crates, bags or boxes'. So if anything the prototype's list is inverted, and main including the poultry, bee, reptile and parrot codes is defensible. What is still unexplained is main's inconsistency inside its own groups: domestic rabbits (01061410) are asked but other rabbits (01061490) are not, and birds of prey, parrots and other birds are asked while ratites (01063300) and pigeons (01063910) are not.

Related, and not this row's to fix: the service collects a package count but never a package type, and the backend sends LogisticsPackage(null, null, totalNoOfPackages) (repos/trade-imports-animals-backend src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/animals/outbox/gbnag/LogisticsPackage.java:12). The GBN-AG schema requires typeCode beside itemQuantity and types it as a string, and that record carries no @JsonInclude(NON_NULL) where its siblings do, so the payload serialises typeCode as an explicit null and fails the schema either way - present-but-null against the string type, or absent against required if NON_NULL were added. Nothing validates the outbox payload against gbn-ag-v1.schema.json anywhere outside the schemas repo, so this is unchecked. Raise it against the GBN-AG payload owner, not here; it matters to this row only in that answering 'which commodities need a package count' may also need 'and what type of package', which no page asks today.

If the ruling goes Design Release 2.1's way, the change is PACKAGE_COUNT_CODES in services/commodities/rules.js plus the consignment-details and check-answers tests that pin the current list. If it goes MDM's way, reference-data must also pass packageType through, which reference-lists owns, so that would add a repo this theme does not have.

increments.title: Species read as their scientific name with the common name in brackets
increments.detail: Every page that lists a species shows the bare Latin name, where it should show the scientific name with the common name in brackets. The MDM commodity search replaced the species label with the Latin name alone, so a trader choosing cattle sees 'Bos taurus' rather than 'Bos taurus (Cattle)'. The data is there: reference-data passes MDM's common name through and the frontend stores it on every line. This row puts the label back across the commodity search, the selected panel, Commodity details, the Selected commodities tables and Identification details, and states the fallback for the species MDM holds no common name for.
acceptanceCriteria: A species reads as its scientific name with the common name in brackets, such as 'Bos taurus (Cattle)', wherever a species is listed: the commodity search results, the selected panel, Commodity details, the Selected commodities tables and Identification details. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-091; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-026; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p5-015)
A species MDM holds no common name for reads as its scientific name alone, with no empty brackets. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-091)
Every new or changed English string has its Welsh counterpart, marked as a machine draft. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p5-044)
notes: Corrected 2 Nov after the re-distil: the label format is the other way round from what this row first said. V4 writes species selections as 'scientific name then common name in brackets' - Bison bison (Bison), Bos spp. (Cattle species), Bos taurus (Cattle), Bubalus bubalis (Water buffalo) (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-091). This row first said 'common name (Latin name)', following Design Release 1 parity (frontend 949bb9d6, 'offer each species as its common name with the Latin name in brackets'). V4 outranks the prototype and the parity work on a field's format, so the Latin name leads. The fallback changes with it: where MDM holds no common name the label is the scientific name alone, not the commodity name in brackets.

Raised by the 2 Nov re-analysis as a regression rather than by a source. speciesLabel returns the Latin name alone (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/species-label.js:1), and it is the one seam every listing goes through, so this is one change in one place plus the tests that followed the regression. The frontend had delivered the common-name format under Design Release 1 parity (frontend 949bb9d6, 'offer each species as its common name with the Latin name in brackets'), and EUDPA-617 replaced it on 27 Oct (c3183a8e).

The data is there: reference-data passes MDM's commonName through (referencedata origin/main:src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/commodities/CommoditySpecies.java:15-20) and the frontend stores speciesCommonName on every line it keeps (features/commodities/search/selection/rows.js:7-24). So no repo beyond the frontend and the tests is needed.

The tests followed the regression rather than catching it, so they change with it: tests origin/main:tests/animals/e2e/pages/consignment-details.spec.ts:91-92 now asserts 'Bos taurus'. Builder: pin the label format in the tests so the next capture or client change cannot drop it again.

The fallback matters more than it looks: many species in MDM's capture hold a null common name (Capreolus, Gazella, Elephas, Kobus, Pholidota and others under 01061900), so a format that assumes a common name would leave those labels bracketed or blank.
inc-013 criterion 1 names the 'common name (Latin name)' label format, so that row rests on this one.

In flight 2 Nov, EUDPA-669: it stores MDM's species commonName on every line and sends it downstream to PIMS, but leaves speciesLabel and legendFor untouched (verified by diff against origin/main). So that ticket confirms and secures this row's data source without doing its display work. Build this row after EUDPA-669 merges, so the stored commonName is already there to read.

increments.title: The frontend's stub commodity fixture matches what the MDM stub serves
increments.detail: Two captures of the same MDM data disagree, so a stub-mode run and a stack run show different species names. The frontend's commodity fixture was captured when the MDM search landed and gives Bos taurus the common name 'Cattle or Cow'. The stub service was corrected the next day to return 'Domestic Cattle' for 0102 and recaptured from TST two days after that, so it now serves 'Domestic Cattle'. The frontend fixture was never recaptured and is behind. Nothing fails today, because no page shows a common name, but the species-label row makes the common name visible, at which point the two disagree in the open. This row recaptures the fixture and adds a check that keeps the two in step.
acceptanceCriteria: The frontend's stub commodity fixture holds the same codes, Latin names and common names as the MDM stub serves through reference-data, so a stub-mode run and a stack run show the same species labels. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p5-064; repo:stub repo-stub-p1-001)
A check fails when the two drift apart, so the next MDM recapture cannot leave the fixture behind without someone noticing. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p5-065)
notes: Raised by the 2 Nov re-analysis rather than by a source. The frontend fixture (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/commodities.json) was captured on 27 Oct with EUDPA-617 (c3183a8e) and gives Bos taurus the common name 'Cattle or Cow'. The stub was corrected on 28 Oct to return 'Domestic Cattle' as the 0102 common name (stub afb74c3) and recaptured from TST on 30 Oct (stub 5cf8a70), so it now gives 'Domestic Cattle'. The frontend fixture has not moved since, so it is three days behind the stub it mirrors.

Nothing is red today because speciesLabel shows the Latin name only, so no common name reaches a page (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/species-label.js:1). inc-025 makes the common name visible, so this row should land with or before it; otherwise stub-mode tests and stack tests assert different words for the same species.

The capture mechanism already exists (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/services/_capture/capture.js and fixtures.js), so the recapture is a run rather than new code. The check is the new part: compare the fixture against what the stub serves, in the frontend's own tests, so it runs without the stack.

increments.title: Remove on Commodity details keeps the numbers the trader has typed but not yet saved
increments.detail: Commodity details collects a number of animals, and a number of packages where the commodity asks for one, per species line. Pressing Remove on one line posts the page, so anything typed into the other lines and not yet saved is lost today. This row keeps it: after a Remove the page comes back with every number the trader had typed still in its field.
acceptanceCriteria: On Commodity details, typing numbers into several species lines and then pressing Remove on one line brings the page back with the numbers typed into the remaining lines still in their fields. (confluence:6497338582; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p8-010)
The removed line is gone from the page and from the saved selection, and the numbers kept are the typed ones rather than the last saved ones. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p5-064)

sources.ref: the Live Animal Data Elements table's number_of_animals_quantity and number_of_packages rows

notes: Pick-up from the 2 November re-distil: req-1759, new since the split. Not blocked.

Main has the seam: the remove action and its post handler sit in features/commodities/consignment-details/remove/actions.js and remove/post-remove.js, and the page's values come through view-model/groups.js, which reads values[animalsField(index)] (frontend origin/main). increments.title: A number of animals beyond what the service can store is refused on its own field
increments.detail: The V4 data fields page caps the number of animals per commodity line at 9,223,372,036,854,775,807, the largest signed 64-bit integer. A number above that cannot be stored, so it is refused on that species' own number of animals field rather than accepted and lost.
acceptanceCriteria: On Commodity details, a number of animals above 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 is refused with an error on that species' number of animals field, and the page keeps what the trader typed. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-102)
A number at or below the cap is accepted and saved. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-102)

sources.ref: confluence-6497338582-p1-102 (Live Animal Data Elements, row number_of_animals_quantity, Type cell)

openQuestions: Is the V4 figure a value cap or a digit count? The same table row writes 'max 9,223,372,036,854,775,807' while its own examples are 25 and 5000, which read as digit counts. The re-distil raised this as its question 5 (c-325) and the default it names is the value cap. If the answer is a digit count, this row's criteria change to a length rule. Who acts: Sam.
notes: Pick-up from the 2 November re-distil: req-2132, new since the split, and the first requirement this programme has taken from V4's Type column rather than from the prototype.

Main validates the number of animals with requiredIntegerInRange(animalsField(index), { min: 1 }) and no maximum (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/fields.js:18-27), so the cap is new. The error belongs on the line's own field, as the animals and packages errors already do.
Build this after question 5 is answered if the answer is quick; otherwise build the default (the value cap) and say so in the commit, since a length rule is a small change on top.

increments.title: The commodity page offers each commodity's types from MDM and narrows the species to them

Choosing a type narrows the species on offer to the species that type covers, and a commodity with no types in MDM asks no type question. (confluence:6497338582)
Every new English string has its Welsh counterpart, marked as a machine draft. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p5-044)

sources.ref: confluence-6497338582-p1-081, -p1-020 (Live Animal Data Elements, row type_selection)

openQuestions: Blocked on reference-data serving MDM's type list. The commodity and species halves of req-2130 are already met: the frontend reads both from reference-data (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/client.js:7-16, and reference-data's CommoditySearchService). notes: Pick-up from the 2 November re-distil: req-2130 and req-2131, both new since the split, combined here because they are one page behaviour over one list. Their pick-up entries read 'Blocked on MDM commodities'; the block is narrowed to the type list alone, because the commodity and species lists arrived with EUDPA-617 on 27 October and that judgement was made against a 26 October repo extract.

Main has a types seam already, but hard-coded rather than from MDM: typeFor and typesFor in services/commodities/rules.js read a TYPES_BY_CODE table holding Domestic and Game for 0102 only, with every other code a single blank type, and the GAME_SPECIES set naming Bos spp. (frontend origin/main:rules.js:82-110). The EUDPA-669 branch widens that set but keeps the table. So this row replaces a local table with MDM's list, the same shape of change inc-012's naming question would need.

Note the Domestic/Game split on 0102 came from the IPAFFS commodity-categories extract rather than from MDM, per the EUDPA-669 branch's own doc, so whoever builds this should check whether MDM's type list reproduces it before deleting the table.
